unusual.text: The velocity row is the rhythm. Every clock plays a step, so a rest is a step turned fully down, and a step half way up is a softer, less punchy hit, not only a quieter one: velocity sets the peak of all three envelopes, pitch and filter as well as loudness, and lengthens their decays a little.
Each PITCH knob spans about ten octaves (±5 V), so a small turn is a big interval. With SEQ PITCH MOD on OFF the row still reaches the PITCH output, a second voltage per step to patch anywhere.

The pitch envelope is bipolar per oscillator: right of centre the pitch spikes up and falls back, the attack of a kick; left of centre it dips and rises back. With both EG AMOUNT knobs at the centre, VCO DECAY seems to do nothing.
Its FM is linear: VCO 1 swings VCO 2’s frequency in hertz around its pitch, so the pitch holds while the sidebands grow, where most synths’ FM bends the pitch.
Noise is wired into the cutoff as well as into the mixer: this knob shakes the filter with it, for dirt and sizzle. A cable in VCF MOD replaces the noise, and is the only direct way into the cutoff.

The clock is an oscillator, 0.7 to 700 Hz, and its TEMPO input is 1 V an octave: a voltage there can stretch single steps (Swing Time) or push the sequencer into audio rate, where it becomes a waveform.
There is no attack knob anywhere: every envelope opens in 1 ms, and only the VCA EG has a second choice, 100 ms, which softens the hit and smooths a sequenced bass line like glide.
Chaining DFAMs is one cable: the first’s TRIGGER OUT into the next’s ADV / CLOCK, with the follower started first.

limits.intro: The whole panel is modelled: both VCOs with their waves, EG amounts, hard sync and linear FM; the three-channel mixer with EXT AUDIO; the ladder filter in LP and HP with its envelope and noise modulation; the three decay envelopes and the VCA; the 8-step sequencer with its clock, RUN / STOP, ADVANCE and TRIGGER; and all 24 patch points with the hardware’s normals.

items.title: Playing it from the keys
items.text: The DFAM has no keyboard and no MIDI. Here the app’s keys stand in for its TRIGGER input and a VCO CV: with the sequencer stopped a key strikes the envelopes at the key’s velocity, and its pitch, from C4, moves both VCOs; while the sequencer runs a key only transposes it. RUN / STOP runs the sequencer on the app’s clock, with Play on the bar, from step 1 on its downbeat; TEMPO chooses how many steps a beat (from about 20 steps a second the clock runs free, as an oscillator).

items.title: What is not modelled
items.text: The rear 1/4-inch output’s headphone and line modes, the Eurorack mounting and the power. The way each analogue unit differs a little from the next. The HP filter’s own resonance scaling, which on the hardware only self-oscillates near 1 kHz: here HP and LP share one scale.

items.title: What the sources leave open
items.text: The manual gives the VCF EG’s decay range, 10 ms to 10 s, but not the VCO and VCA EGs’: here they share it. It says velocity lengthens the decays slightly but not by how much: here full velocity lengthens them by 15 %. The pitch envelope’s and VCF EG’s depth at full, the 1→2 FM depth, the VCOs’ centre (C3 here) and the tapers are the app’s. The manual says both that velocity sets the envelopes’ amplitude and that it changes their decay; both are modelled. A clock into ADV / CLOCK moves the sequencer only while it runs, as the manual’s sync instructions start the follower first. Knob positions are read 7 o’clock = 0 to 5 o’clock = 10, and −5 to +5 for the bipolar ones.
